title: SOURCE_TARGETS validated: Fast ADMIN CHECK TABLE leaks optimizer invisible-index state

payload.user_symptom: In one session, after SET SESSION tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes=ON, ADMIN CHECK TABLE with fast check enabled keeps @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes displayed as ON but the next query no longer uses an invisible index. The same SELECT plan changes from IndexReader/IndexRangeScan to TableReader/TableFullScan.
payload.validation_scope: Reproduced on dedicated testbed 8220955 running 8.0.11-TiDB-v9.0.0-beta.2.pre-1895-g5c9198e948 through SQL only. A fast-check-off control keeps the plan on the invisible index, which localizes the fault to the fast check path.
payload.quality_gate: High-quality user-visible behavior: no contract ambiguity, no fault injection, and a same-session plan oracle observes behavior drift while @@ variable display remains ON.
payload.method_pivot: The dynamic STATE_INGRESS_INTERNAL_SQL target did not fail via pending TxnReadTS. It exposed a stronger nearby proof obligation: helper fast paths that temporarily override user session state must restore the exact prior value.

provenance.source: state-ingress dynamic target plus SQL-only testbed reproduction

name: Temporary helper changes to user session state must restore the exact prior value

query_pattern: code reads a user session field P
code temporarily overwrites P to force a helper or fast path
cleanup writes a constant or partial restore instead of restoring the previous value
a later user statement observes behavior inconsistent with the user's session setting
code_markers: direct assignment to e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().* before helper work
defer writes a constant value rather than a saved old value
nearby code has a backup/restore helper for sys session variables, suggesting restoration is expected
SQL variable display and optimizer behavior can diverge if the field is changed directly
stop_rules: require a same-session after-observation, not just a source assignment
prefer behavior oracle over @@ variable oracle when sysvar display and internal fields can diverge
run a fast-path-off or feature-off control to localize the fault

name: Fast ADMIN CHECK TABLE session-state override

state_model: buildCheckTable selects FastCheckTableExec when tidb_enable_fast_table_check is ON and the table indexes are eligible
FastCheckTableExec.Next directly sets the user session OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes field to true so all indexes, including invisible indexes, are checked
the deferred cleanup writes OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes=false instead of restoring the user's previous value
worker code separately obtains sys sessions and has proper backup/restore helpers for sys session variables, so the user-session cleanup bug is on the outer fast check executor
after cleanup, @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes can still print ON while optimizer behavior follows the directly mutated false field
source_anchors: pkg/executor/builder.go:538-556 builds FastCheckTableExec when FastCheckTable is enabled
pkg/executor/check_table_index.go:288-298 sets OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes=true and defers a hard reset to false
pkg/executor/check_table_index.go:340-381 shows the sys-session variable backup/restore pattern used elsewhere in the same file
pkg/executor/check_table_index.go:474-496 worker obtains a sys session and initializes it from the user session
pkg/executor/internal/exec/executor.go:568-591 GetSysSession/ReleaseSysSession use the domain sys session pool

name: Fast ADMIN CHECK TABLE must preserve the user's invisible-index optimizer setting

payload.p_check: FastCheckTableExec.Next overwrites e.Ctx().GetSessionVars().OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes=true and defers setting it to false.
payload.q_claim: ADMIN CHECK TABLE may temporarily enable invisible indexes for its own consistency check, but it must leave the user's session optimizer behavior unchanged after the statement completes.
payload.fault: the defer hard-resets OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes to false instead of restoring the pre-statement value.

boundary.before: user sets tidb_enable_fast_table_check=ON and tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes=ON, then an EXPLAIN on an invisible-index predicate uses IndexReader/IndexRangeScan
boundary.fault: user runs ADMIN CHECK TABLE on the table; fast check temporarily flips OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes and hard-resets it to false
boundary.after: @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes still displays 1, but the same EXPLAIN switches to TableReader/TableFullScan

source_anchors: pkg/sessionctx/vardef/tidb_vars.go:1019-1020 maps the user-facing variable to tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes

name: Session variable behavior remains consistent after an admin helper statement

payload.contract: A statement that temporarily changes optimizer session state for internal checking must restore the previous value so later statements behave as if the user's session setting is unchanged.
minimal_observation: create a table with an invisible index on v
control before: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM t WHERE v=20 uses the invisible index
RED if @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes still shows ON but the same EXPLAIN no longer uses the invisible index

red_signature.before_lines: lines 3-7 show use_invisible=1, fast_check=1, and IndexReader/IndexRangeScan
red_signature.after_lines: lines 8-13 show use_invisible=1, fast_check=1, then TableReader/TableFullScan

control_signature.observation: with tidb_enable_fast_table_check=OFF, the same before/after EXPLAIN remains IndexReader/IndexRangeScan

name: ADMIN CHECK TABLE after enabling invisible-index optimizer use

payload.shape: The user intentionally enables invisible-index planning in a session, runs an administrative consistency check, then continues using the same session for normal queries.
payload.why_interesting: The admin helper has a valid reason to force invisible indexes internally, so the bug only appears if the oracle checks the user's next statement behavior rather than the helper's own result.
setup: temporary table with an invisible secondary index
same-session EXPLAIN before and after ADMIN CHECK TABLE
controls: @@ variable display plus behavior oracle to catch display/behavior divergence

name: Session variable, helper statement, then same-session behavior oracle

steps: create a feature-specific object whose use depends on a session variable
set the session variable to a non-default value
record a behavior oracle before the helper statement
run the candidate helper or admin statement
record both @@ variable display and behavior oracle afterward
repeat with the helper fast path disabled if possible
red_conditions: the post-helper behavior changes despite the user variable display remaining unchanged
the disabled-fast-path control does not show the behavior drift
green_conditions: after a fix, the same session keeps both display and behavior consistent with the pre-helper setting

lessons.selector_worked_but_pivoted: The source target was queued for internal-SQL state ingress, but source inspection exposed an adjacent direct user-session state mutation. Following the proof obligation rather than the original label found a stronger bug.
lessons.oracle_strength: Reading @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes alone was too weak and falsely looked green. The behavior oracle with an invisible index caught display/behavior divergence.
lessons.quality_note: No product-contract ambiguity: an administrative helper should not silently change later optimizer behavior in the same session.

evidence.control_observation: with fast check disabled, before and after ADMIN CHECK TABLE both use IndexReader/IndexRangeScan on invisible idx_v, while @@tidb_opt_use_invisible_indexes remains 1

lessons.localization: The behavior drift requires the fast check path and is not an inherent effect of ADMIN CHECK TABLE.
lessons.method_note: Feature-off controls are cheap high-value oracles when a source target points at a fast path.
